ideas.topic: Why Ancient Egyptians Wore Cones of Fat on Their Heads
ideas.hook: You’ve seen the statues with strange, melting cones on their heads, but do you know they were actually made of solid scented animal fat?
ideas.why: It leverages the 'curiosity gap' regarding mysterious historical beauty standards, similar to the high-performing 'Beards or Clean-Shaven' video.

ideas.topic: The Secret Purpose of the 'False Door' in Tombs
ideas.hook: This stone door looks like it leads to another room, but it was actually a portal for the soul to pass between the living and the dead.
ideas.why: It focuses on the architectural mystery of the pyramids and tombs, tapping into the audience's interest in the 'Impossible Problem' of ancient engineering.

ideas.topic: The Real Reason Egyptians Honored the Scarab Beetle
ideas.hook: It’s just a dung beetle, yet the most powerful pharaohs wore it as their most sacred symbol—here is why.
ideas.why: Animal-related Egyptian history has proven high engagement on your channel; this connects the mundane (insects) to the grand (pharaonic power).
